LESSON: SETTING TEXT TO MUSIC

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Foundations of Music and Dance
Topic 1.4: Setting Text to Music
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 11

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Setting Text to Music, part of Foundations of Music and Dance in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How are pitches assigned to different words to communicate messages clearly? 2. How does text dictate composition of a melody?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Setting Text to Music together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: The learner speaks clearly as they discuss factors that guide syllabic

division and accentuation of text in Kiswahili.

● Creativity and imagination: The learner adds appropriate pitches to the syllables while paying attention to word

painting, melodic contour, range and overall structure.

● Citizenship: The learner participates in community service by composing music in Kiswahili with messages to

sensitize the community members.

● Learning to learn: The learner applies compositional skills on song writing to compose music for given text.

● Digital literacy: The learner uses music notation software to compose and playback music.

Core competencies to be developed:


  -  Communication and collaboration: The learner speaks clearly as they discuss factors that guide syllabic

division and accentuation of text in Kiswahili.


  -  Creativity and imagination: The learner adds appropriate pitches to the syllables while paying attention to word

painting, melodic contour, range and overall structure.


  -  Citizenship: The learner participates in community service by composing music in Kiswahili with messages to

sensitize the community members.


  -  Learning to learn: The learner applies compositional skills on song writing to compose music for given text.


  -  Digital literacy: The learner uses music notation software to compose and playback music.

Values:


  -  Respect: The learner appreciates others’ views when giving and receiving feedback on their compositions.


  -  Responsibility: The learner uses digital devices with appropriate assistive technology for the intended purpose.


  -  Social justice: The learner shares learning resources with others when creating music.


  -  Patriotism: The learners promote good health in the community by composing music to sensitize community

members in healthy practices.

15

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCI
s) :


  -  Road safety: the learner selects text in Kiswahili on pertinent and contemporary issues such as regulation for

road users.


  -  Communicable diseases: the learner composes music to sensitize the populace on communicable diseases.


  -  Waste management: the learner creates a text on waste management to sensitize the community on

environmental cleanliness.


  -  Healthy relationships: the learners collaborate with each other in group work as they build peaceable

relationships among each other.


  -  Financial literacy: the learner selects text in Kiswahili on pertinent and contemporary issues such as financial

literacy.
